summary.text: Presents the opening section of WHO Summary Table 2 (updated December 2025) detailing minimum age of first dose, number of primary doses, inter-dose intervals, booster doses, and key considerations for universally recommended childhood vaccines: RSV (maternal vaccination or newborn monoclonal antibody), BCG, Hepatitis B, and Polio (bOPV+IPV preferred, early, hexavalent, sequential IPV/bOPV, and 3-dose or post-cessation 2-dose IPV-only schedules).

blocks.title: Front matter
blocks.content:
Refer to https://www.who.int/teams/immunization-vaccines-and-biologicals/policies/position-papers for latest position paper updates. 
This table summarizes the WHO vaccination recommendations for children. The ages/intervals cited are for the development of country specific schedules and are not for health workers. 
National schedules should be based on local epidemiologic, programmatic, resource & policy considerations. While vaccines are universally recommended, some children may have contraindications to particular vaccines. 
 
 
              P.1 / 14 
(updated: December 2025)

summary.text: Provides the introductory header and disclaimer for WHO's December 2025 Summary Table 2 on recommended routine immunizations for children, noting that the cited ages and dose intervals are intended to guide country-specific schedule development based on local epidemiologic, programmatic, resource, and policy considerations.

summary.text: Completes WHO Summary Table 2 (updated December 2025) with childhood dosing schedules for regional, high-risk, and programme-specific vaccines—Japanese Encephalitis, Yellow Fever, Tick-Borne Encephalitis, Typhoid, Cholera, Meningococcal, Hepatitis A, Rabies, Dengue (TAK-003), Malaria, Mumps, Seasonal Influenza, Varicella, and the alternative 1p+1 PCV schedule—followed by comprehensive footnotes (1–24) detailing WHO position paper guidance for each antigen.
